channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Zelenskyy warns Russia is preparing new strikes; five hurt in an attack on central Kyiv
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · In his nightly address, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia preparing new strikes, and asked the US and other partners to take note because their decisions affect air-defence supplies, per Reuters. A Russian attack on central Kyiv on Monday injured five people. French President Macron said "we must reopen the question of Ukraine's membership to NATO". No date has been set for the next round of talks, and the agreed prisoner exchange has not been reported as carried out.

item.title: Russia and NATO: NATO sends a radar plane to Poland; Russia warns Estonia of 'open war'
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · NATO ambassadors met in Brussels, and NATO's top military commander ordered an AWACS early-warning radar plane to Poland. NATO said Russia "bears full responsibility" for the missiles. Poland did not formally ask for Article 4 talks this time. The same day Russia's foreign ministry summoned Estonia's acting envoy in Moscow and said Estonia was "on the verge of triggering open war". Estonia denied letting Ukraine use its airspace.

item.title: Budget 2027: Finance Minister holds 10 rounds of pre-Budget talks
item.description: 17–23 Nov 2026 · Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has now held 10 pre-Budget meetings. Since 17 November she met groups from manufacturing; small businesses and startups; capital markets, banking and insurance; IT; infrastructure, energy and sustainability; jobs and labour; housing, cities and culture; and, on 23 November, health and social sectors. The ministry has not said what was suggested. The Budget is expected on 1 February 2027.

item.title: Delhi air: Monday morning AQI 236, 'poor'; air commission sets a 15–20% pollution-cut target for 2027
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI was 236 ('poor') at 8 am on Monday, per CPCB data reported by IANS. Some stations were 'very poor', including Sirifort (333), Talkatora (317) and ITO (301). Stage II curbs stay in force. The Commission for Air Quality Management told Delhi and nearby states to write 2027 action plans that cut overall pollution by at least 15%, aiming for 20%. For the first time the plans must include district-level plans and name the officers responsible. Forecasts expect 'poor' air until Wednesday, then 'poor' to 'very poor'.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Nvidia shares close about 31% higher; Trump says "I convinced them", while lawmakers in both parties question the decision
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia shares rose about 31% on Monday, their biggest one-day gain since 2003, adding about $950 billion in market value, per Investopedia. They are still about 31% below their 6 October high. President Trump told CNBC "I convinced them" and called the board's decision "an absolutely GREAT decision" on Truth Social. Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats would investigate; Jeffries called the decision "indefensible". Several Republican senators also questioned it: Senator John Curtis asked "what changed" while the board's own investigation is still running. A House Intelligence Committee spokesperson said the reinstatement "changes nothing" for Huang's appearance before House committees on 1 December. Senate Banking Committee chair Tim Scott has asked for public testimony, with a hearing reported for 3 December. Nvidia's filing also says a new board committee on national security and export controls is hiring outside lawyers, and the company is searching for a new chief compliance officer.

item.title: AI this week: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang; AI shares lead Wall Street's biggest rally since April 2025
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, saying senior US officials told it his return poses no national security risk. Nvidia shares rose about 31% and the Nasdaq 6.51%. Anthropic shares slipped. The same weekend, OpenAI's chief scientist proposed shared limits across AI labs, OpenAI made GPT-6.2 Sol the main ChatGPT model for paying users, and Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX over sexual deepfakes made with Grok.

item.title: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Sol becomes the main model in ChatGPT for paying users
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · A version of GPT-6.2 Sol tuned for everyday conversation is rolling out in ChatGPT's Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users. Free and Go users are not included yet, and no date was given for them. In OpenAI's own tests it follows its safety policies in difficult conversations 91–94% of the time, up from 77–80% for GPT-6.

item.title: Anthropic: Shares slip on day three while the rest of tech rallies
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares fell on Monday while Nvidia and most tech shares jumped. CNBC, cited by FinanceFeeds, put the fall at 1.43%; ABC News said it was more than 1%. The shares stayed above the $83 IPO price. Yahoo Finance pointed to profit-taking after the listing, doubts about the valuation, and up to 315 million shares held by insiders that can be sold almost straight away.

item.title: xAI & Grok: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over sexual deepfakes made with Grok
item.description: 22–23 Nov 2026 · The attorneys general of Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX, which owns xAI and X, under consumer-protection laws. They allege Grok's "spicy mode" was used to make sexualised images of real people, including children, and that the companies misled users about safety. They seek penalties, repayments and court orders. SpaceX did not comment. X's safety team has said it blocks such requests and that users who made them broke its rules. The court has not ruled.

item.title: Starship: Mexico says SpaceX must take responsibility for suspected debris near Matamoros
item.description: 21–23 Nov 2026 · Mexican authorities said SpaceX must take responsibility for suspected rocket debris washing up on beaches near Matamoros, across the border from Starbase, per Texas Public Radio and the Texas Tribune. An environmental group, Conibio Global, says it has found at least 1,500 fragments that look like plastic, rubber and adhesive, and believes they came from the Flight 15 booster; it says this still needs confirming. A dead sea turtle is being examined. Mexico's environment agency, Profepa, told people not to touch fragments. SpaceX said on 19 November that its partners found "very little debris" and called claims of widespread damage "outright fabrications or intentionally misleading". No date has been announced for Flight 16.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Brent falls to its lowest since late August as Gulf exports hold up
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Brent crude settled near $86.6–86.8 a barrel on Monday, its lowest since late August, down from $92.57 on Friday. US crude (WTI) closed around $79–80. Analysts said signs that Gulf crude exports are holding up outweighed weekend attacks on shipping and on Bahrain, per Investing.com and Tradingpedia. Libya's Sharara pipeline also reopened. The International Energy Agency expects supply to exceed demand by about 2 million barrels a day in October–December. Analysts at IG said a new US strike on Iran looks less likely for now. Lower oil prices help India, which imports most of its crude.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran vows to confront the US blockade; says Hormuz could be safe again if its terms are met
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran would "definitely not tolerate" the US naval blockade and would "use all our tools" to confront it, per ABC News. He said security in the Strait of Hormuz could be restored quickly if the US lifts sanctions, ends the blockade and carries out the terms of the June memorandum of understanding. Oil shipped through Hormuz averaged about 9.5 million barrels a day in the 10 days to 19 November, down from 12.2 million in October, per Kpler data cited by Reuters. Iran began rationing electricity on 22 November because of fuel shortages, ABC reports.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three more tankers hit mines in Hormuz despite a US escort
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The navy of Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said on Monday that three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz over the previous few hours, per Iranian state media cited by Iran International. It said one was hit near the southern coast and two east of the strait, and that a US military escort failed to prevent this. "The Strait of Hormuz is not a place to test unauthorized routes or ignore maritime warnings," the IRGC said. The ships were not named and no casualties were reported. The claim has not been independently confirmed, and US Central Command had not responded at the time of reporting, per The Sunday Guardian. This is a separate claim from Iran's report on Sunday of two tankers hitting mines.

item.title: West Asia & oil: US sanctions 22 companies and 8 people it links to Iran's oil money networks
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The US Treasury announced new sanctions on Monday against 22 entities and eight individuals it says help move money for Iran's oil trade and tanker fleet, per gCaptain and Iran International. Most of the companies named are in Dubai, with others in Hong Kong and Turkey, Iran International reports. Sanctions bar them from dealing with US banks and businesses. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said "Iran's shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime," per Iran International. A separate Treasury analysis found $14.7 billion in transactions that may be linked to these networks, it reports.

item.title: US trade deal: Farmers' groups plan protests on 26 November against the US trade deal
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The Samyukta Kisan Morcha, a coalition of farmers' unions, says farmers will march in Delhi, from Mandir Marg to Jantar Mantar, and protest at about 100 other places on 26 November. They want India to drop the proposed trade deal with the US and other free trade agreements. Farm leaders say cheaper US farm imports would hurt Indian farmers. The government has not announced a signing date.

item.title: US markets: S&P 500 jumps 4.7% after Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang, ending a seven-day losing run
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, its best day since April 2025, per Investopedia (via Yahoo Finance). Its 327-point rise was its second-biggest ever in points. The Dow rose 3.01% to 49,595.31 and the Nasdaq 6.51% to 24,089.56. Before the open, Nvidia said its board had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Nvidia shares rose about 31%, their biggest one-day gain since 2003, and added about $950 billion in market value. Reporters also pointed to forced buying by traders who had bet on further falls, lower oil prices, and Oracle saying it has the funding it needs for its OpenAI computing deal. A Nomura strategist called it a "mechanical" bounce that does not settle worries about inflation, borrowing costs and AI spending. Anthropic shares fell on the day, by 1.43% per CNBC. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; the SPY fund that tracks the S&P 500 opened about 5% higher, per Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Ukraine says its sea drones hit a Russian warship in a Libyan port, 2,400 km from the front
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · President Zelenskyy said on 23 November that Ukrainian sea drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi, eastern Libya, on Sunday 22 November. He said seven drones were used, a helicopter on board was destroyed, and a cargo ship, the Angara, was also hit; he said Russia used it to move weapons. Ukraine's security service (SBU) said the drones were launched from a "mother ship". At least 10 people were wounded, including Libyans and Russians, per AP. Libya's eastern government asked the UN for an investigation. The Kremlin said it had "taken note". The site is about 2,400 km from the front line. Separately, a Russian oil refinery in Rostov stopped work after a Ukrainian drone attack, its regional governor said.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Drones hit Russian ships in the Gulf of Finland and in a Libyan port
item.description: 21–22 Nov 2026 · On 21 November drones hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland; all 16 crew were evacuated, per Al Jazeera. Kyiv has not claimed that attack. On 22 November Ukrainian sea drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya, President Zelenskyy said the next day, about 2,400 km from the front line. Libya's eastern government asked the UN for an investigation.

item.title: SpiceJet: SpiceJet reported to be flying 10–15 flights a day, while tickets stay on sale for cancelled routes
item.description: 21–22 Nov 2026 · SpiceJet is flying about 10–15 flights a day, against about 66 a day in its winter schedule, the Free Press Journal reports. At least eight Delhi–Mumbai flights each way were cancelled from 19 to 21 November, and a Mumbai–Dubai flight that had not flown for about a week was still on sale, it says. Passengers quoted by the paper say refunds have not arrived 20 days after cancellation; DGCA rules require card refunds within seven days. More than 7,000 complaints are on the government's AirSewa portal, PTI reports, per Millennium Post. SpiceJet has not commented on the ticket sales. No public reply to the DGCA's show-cause notice had been reported by 23 November.

item.title: OpenAI: Chief scientist proposes shared limits across AI labs, publishing internal 'perplexity' scores
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published the company's internal "perplexity" scores for the first time. The score measures how well a model predicts the next piece of text; lower means more capable. He proposed that AI labs agree on common limits, based on this and other measures, that they would not cross until tools to understand and monitor AI behaviour reach a set level. No other lab has signed up and nothing is binding. Critics say other labs cannot reproduce or compare the scores.

item.title: Anthropic: A readable draft of the Claude-assisted Riemann proof appears; it is unfinished and the key step is not yet written out
item.description: 21–22 Nov 2026 · A University of Waterloo mathematician posted a working draft of about 160 pages explaining the computer-checked proof in ordinary maths language. The draft says it was written by Claude, OpenAI's Codex and Google's Gemini at his request. It says it is unfinished: it does not yet prove the "main inequality", which it calls "the arithmetic heart" of the proof, and quotes it from the Lean code instead. The Decoder reports that mathematicians are still checking whether the Lean statement matches the Riemann Hypothesis exactly. A separate, human-written draft proof of a related conjecture, posted on Stanford professor Ravi Vakil's blog on 20 November, drew reports of problems within hours. Neither proof has been accepted.

item.title: US midterms: AP calls North Carolina's 5th district for Democrat Chuck Hubbard after a recount
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · AP called North Carolina's 5th House district for Democrat Chuck Hubbard after a recount, per ABC News. The seat had been held by Republican Virginia Foxx since 2005. Foxx conceded on Sunday, writing that voters "made their voices heard", per WRAL. Before the recount Hubbard led by 331 votes out of more than 286,000, in the unofficial state count. Some other House races are still being counted.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Three Russian cruise missiles come down in south-east Poland
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Three objects fell in south-east Poland during a large Russian attack on Ukraine. Polish prosecutors in Lublin said on 22 November that all three were Kh-101 cruise missiles, per Notes from Poland. They were in Polish airspace for about three minutes, and no one was hurt. Prime Minister Tusk called it an apparent "intentional provocation", timed to a military exercise in Poland. NATO's Rutte would not say whether it was deliberate. Russia had not commented.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Denmark expels Russia's defence attaché over an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Denmark's intelligence service (PET) said Russian intelligence planned to have a Ukrainian-American rapper killed at a concert near Copenhagen, using a banned Danish gang. Two Danish men were charged with attempted murder; both reportedly deny it. Denmark gave Russia's defence attaché seven days to leave. Russia's embassy called the expulsion "vengeful" and said Denmark had shown no evidence.

item.title: Flying this winter: Airlines schedule 3.5% fewer domestic flights for November–December
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · Indian airlines plan 195,774 domestic flights in November and December 2026, 7,154 fewer than a year earlier, or about 117 fewer a day, per Cirium schedule data first reported by the Indian Express. It is the first such fall since 2022. Air India's schedule is down 15.9% and SpiceJet's 25.3%; IndiGo's is down 1.7% and Akasa's up 46.9%. Seats fall only 0.5%, because some airlines are using bigger planes. These are published schedules, so the number of flights actually flown may be lower. Fewer flights in the holiday season can mean fuller planes and higher fares.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Estonia blames Russian military intelligence for an arson attempt and moves to close its border
item.description: 14–15 Nov 2026 · Estonia's Internal Security Service said Russia's military intelligence (GRU) ordered an attempted arson attack on a drone maker near Tallinn on 14 November, the second such attempt on a defence company since August. Eight Latvian citizens were detained. On 15 November the government moved to close its three road crossings with Russia, at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, from 1 December. Russia denies involvement.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Russian missile explodes in a field in eastern Poland
item.description: 30 Jul 2026 · A missile came down in eastern Poland during a Russian attack on western Ukraine, leaving a crater about 10 metres wide. No one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it was likely a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile. NATO scrambled fighter jets, and Secretary General Mark Rutte called it "yet another reckless act by Russia".

item.title: Russia and NATO: Poland calls emergency NATO talks after Russian drones enter its airspace
item.description: 10 Sep 2025 · Several Russian drones crossed into Poland during an attack on Ukraine. Polish and Dutch fighter jets shot some of them down. Poland invoked Article 4 of NATO's treaty, which lets a member call emergency talks with allies when it feels threatened.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: ABC: the woman at the centre of the reports was in touch with a Chinese spy agency official
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · ABC News, citing sources familiar with US intelligence, reported that the woman whose relationship with Jensen Huang started the affair kept in contact with an official at China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until this autumn. ABC credits The New York Times with reporting this first. It says it is not clear whether US intelligence shows she passed on inside information. She left Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company, in 2025, a company spokesperson told ABC. China has denied that she spied for it, per Reuters. The White House and State Department did not immediately respond to ABC.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia said its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The board said it held talks with Huang and was "satisfied" with his "candor and ability to lead". It said it had received input from "senior levels of the United States government" and is confident his return "poses no national security risk". It did not name the officials. The board committee's investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort will continue to its conclusion, and Huang said he would cooperate. Colette Kress, the interim CEO, stays chief financial officer, and Harvey Jones stays board chair. Reuters notes the board had ruled out his return days earlier, on 17 November. Nvidia shares rose more than 25% in trading before the US market opened, per Reuters.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee slips back past 93 as Indian shares fall
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The rupee settled at 92.62 per dollar on Friday, PTI reports. On Monday it opened at 93.47, briefly strengthened to 92.43, then fell back to 92.85 in early trade. Forex traders told PTI that cheaper oil helped at first, but a firm US dollar and selling in Indian shares weighed on it. By 12:30 pm it had fallen to 93.08, the day's low, per Business Standard, as the Sensex dropped about 1.1% by midday. These are intraday levels; the closing rate may differ.

item.title: India markets: Banks and metals drag Nifty down 1.75% after a higher open
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened higher and traded near 25,872 in the first minutes, according to Business Standard. It then fell through the day to close down 450.95 points (1.75%) at 25,349.65, according to Kotak Neo and Univest. The Sensex fell 1,483.72 points (1.77%) to 82,435.99. Both reports blame selling in bank and metal stocks and profit-taking. Univest calls it profit-taking after a four-week rally and also points to price swings ahead of the monthly expiry of derivative contracts. Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35 and Nifty Metal fell 3.68%, while Nifty IT rose 1.69%, per Univest and Kotak Neo. Univest says a Tata Steel deal with APL Apollo Tubes weighed on metal shares. Tata Steel (−8.43%) fell the most in the Nifty and TCS (+3.53%) gained the most, per Univest. The India VIX, a gauge of expected price swings, rose 4.04% to 18.02.

item.title: COP31 climate talks: COP31 ends with no main agreement
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · The final text referred to the 2023 agreement on moving away from fossil fuels without naming them, and kept support for carbon capture, per AFP and ABC Australia. The EU said it could not accept a text with no reference to fossil fuels, Panama rejected it and the Marshall Islands withheld support, per UN News, so the main decision was not adopted. "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Kurum said. ABC Australia says the summit ended 44 hours after its official close, the longest UN climate summit on record, and that Russia and Saudi Arabia backed leaving fossil fuels out. Bowen called the outcome "very disappointing". UN Secretary-General António Guterres said: "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."

item.title: COP31 climate talks: India says it engaged constructively and regrets the lack of consensus
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said India "engaged constructively" until the end and regretted that no consensus was reached, per PTI. "Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology," he said, adding that past emissions by rich countries "have consumed a disproportionate share of the global carbon budget". India sided with developing countries pressing for more climate finance.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russian strikes on Kyiv region hit an apartment block and a supermarket; Zelenskyy asks the US for Patriot missiles
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · A Russian strike early on Sunday destroyed part of a five-storey apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv. At least three people were killed and four wounded, per AP and the Kyiv regional governor via Ukrinform, and about a dozen were still believed trapped. On Sunday evening a drone hit a supermarket in the Vyshneve area of Kyiv region, killing at least two people and injuring eight, the governor said, per the Kyiv Independent. He declared 23 November a day of mourning in the region. Zelenskyy said Russia launched about 2,700 attack drones, nearly 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles over the past week, and urged the US to approve delivery of Patriot air-defence missiles that partners have already paid for, per Al Jazeera. No new talks or prisoner exchange were reported.

item.title: Delhi air: Sunday's daily AQI 239, 'poor'; forecast warns of 'very poor' air later in the week
item.description: 22 Nov 2026, daily average · Delhi's average AQI for Sunday was 239, in the 'poor' band (201–300), down from 265 on Saturday, per CPCB figures reported by The Pioneer and Daily Jagran. Of 56 stations, 8 were 'very poor', 36 'poor' and 12 'moderate'; the worst were Uttam Nagar (332) and IGNOU Maidan Garhi (330). Daily Jagran reports that vehicles caused 38.6% of PM2.5 pollution on Sunday, the largest share. The air-quality early warning system expects 'poor' air from Monday to Wednesday, then 'poor' to 'very poor' for the six days after, as weaker winds disperse pollution less. No change to GRAP curbs was reported; Stage I and II stay.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran says two supertankers hit mines east of Hormuz; UKMTO reports a tanker 'incident with military forces'
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Iran's navy said on Sunday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the ships had switched off their tracking systems and entered a 'forbidden' area, per Xinhua. The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) navy separately said two supertankers exploded on 'unauthorized' routes north of Oman's Al Ghanam Island. The ships were not named and no one else has confirmed the incident. On Sunday evening UKMTO, the British agency that tracks shipping, said a tanker 'was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman', near Chabahar, and that investigations were under way, per Euronews. It gave no ship name or casualties. Euronews says the area is near the US blockade line, but it is not known whether this involved one of the Iranian tankers said to be ready to test the blockade. The IRGC also said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone east of the strait; the US has not commented.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Trump says he could resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail
item.description: 21–22 Nov 2026 (US time) · In a Fox News interview, President Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail, per Arab Times and Iran International. Asked about Iranian tankers testing the US blockade, he said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," per Arab Times. Iran International quotes him as saying: "I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent." Indirect talks continue, with Qatar passing messages, Arab Times reports. Iran's parliament speaker said a state of 'neither war nor peace' cannot continue, and a deputy foreign minister said Iran is still talking to the US but is ready for any scenario, per Iran International. No decision to strike has been announced.

item.title: US midterms: Van Hollen claims growing support in his challenge to Schumer; Trump weighs in
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 (US time) · Senator Chris Van Hollen, who launched a challenge to Chuck Schumer for leader of the Senate Democrats on 12 November, told NBC's Meet the Press that more than 15 senators back him, per Newsweek and HNGN. Newsweek's count of public statements has at least 16 senators backing Schumer and 6 backing Van Hollen. The vote is a secret ballot on 1 December; 28 of 55 eligible senators-elect are needed to win. On Truth Social, President Trump wrote: "It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader."

item.title: COP31 climate talks: Talks run into overtime as fossil fuels vanish from the draft deal
item.description: 20–21 Nov 2026 · The summit ran past its scheduled close on Friday 20 November. An early draft of the main decision, released in the second week, repeated the 2023 COP28 pledge to transition away from fossil fuels, per Forbes and Al Jazeera. A shorter later draft removed every mention of coal, oil and gas, and dropped a $120 billion target for adaptation finance, money to help poorer countries cope with climate impacts, per AFP and Forbes. AFP reports Saudi Arabia resisted strong fossil-fuel language; Al Jazeera says Saudi Arabia and other big oil and gas producers objected. Panama's environment minister said: "We are being held hostage by the petroleum mafia," per Forbes. Late on Saturday Kurum told delegates: "We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon."
